title: Watson on Sketching in Public
content: Ernest Watson, in his bookThe Art of Pencil Drawing, says "One has to become accustomed to a reasonable amount of attention from curious pedestrians."Pennsylvania Station, Pittsburgh, pencil drawing by Ernest Watson"You become a public entertainer as soon as you establish yourself in a public place. You have no right to privacy. You get used to this, in time, and should not be disturbed by respectful onlookers. When possible, seek a semi-secluded nook or at least a wall, against which you can sit and enjoy a degree of privacy.The famous Rialto in Venice is a very busy thoroughfare," he continues. "The artist is practically forced to seek a reasonably quiet spot out of the traffic flow. When I went to draw the Rialto, there was but one such place for a favored view of the bridge, and this spot seemed constantly occupied by other artists. I found it vacant after three or four visits to the place."----FromThe Art of Pencil Drawingby Ernest Watson
